brief: GS forecasts October nonfarm payrolls rose 75k, above consensus of 65k and the three-month average of 51k, and private payrolls rose 70k vs consensus 64k. The call rests on three supporting factors: low layoffs (initial claims averaging 198k, down from 204k in September; JOLTS layoff rate down 0.1pp to 1.0%), solid big-data signals averaging roughly 70k job growth, and residual seasonality, since September's late Labor Day typically depresses that month's print (September payrolls were 29k) and October typically rebounds by about 50k. Weighing against a stronger report, employer survey employment components softened (manufacturing -0.5pt to 52.6, services -0.8pt to 50.8), though GS discounts survey signals as unreliable post-pandemic. Job openings and the labor differential were roughly stable to slightly higher. GS forecasts average hourly earnings up 0.3% m/m, in line with consensus, on neutral calendar effects; its wage tracker rose 3.0% q/q annualized and 3.3% y/y in Q3. GS forecasts the unemployment rate unchanged at 4.2%, in line with consensus, but sees risk skewed toward a lower reading as continuing claims imply a lower level. Its slack tracker, still at 4.6%, suggests the labor market is somewhat softer than the unemployment rate alone implies.
